title: Define model metadata schema v1 + add validation tooling (fixtures + CI)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Model Metadata Schema + Automated Changelog Generator
description:
Context / problem
Today model/version information is split across the model registry, runtime config, and docs/release processes. This causes:
- Customer-facing changes shipped without consistent release notes
- Support unable to answer “what changed?” quickly during regressions
- Rollout policies (eligibility, fallbacks, compatibility) relying on ad-hoc fields

ENG-9821 delivers the formal model metadata schema v1 + validation tooling needed to make the registry the source of truth for model/variant/version metadata.

Goals
1) Define metadata schema v1 with clear required fields for launch and documented invariants.
2) Provide a machine-validated contract (JSON Schema) + fixtures for common model families.
3) Add CI validation so metadata changes cannot land without:
   - Schema validity
   - Required fields present
   - Compatibility constraints parse + validate
   - Public vs internal field boundaries preserved (no “internal-only” leakage into public artifacts)

Non-goals
- Migration/backfill (tracked in ENG-9822)
- Changelog generation pipeline (ENG-9823)
- Console UI surfaces (ENG-9824)

Design / references
- Confluence: Model metadata schema v1: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/model-metadata-schema-v1.json
- ADR: Source of truth + publishing rules: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0142-model-metadata-source-of-truth-and-publishing.json
- ADR: Changelog generation approach: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0143-changelog-generation-from-events-vs-git-tags.json
- Editorial taxonomy (for downstream generator): sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/customer-release-notes-taxonomy-and-style-guide.json

Schema v1: requirements (must-have for MVP)
Required top-level identifiers
- model_id: stable registry identifier (immutable)
- display_name: customer-facing name
- publisher: e.g., “meta”, “mistral”, “redwood-verified” (enum/list)
- model_family: used for grouping (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen)

Versioning + lifecycle
- version: semantic version string (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
  - MAJOR increments: breaking changes for typical workloads and/or compat constraints change
  - MINOR: non-breaking improvements (quality/perf/bugfix) or expanded hardware support
  - PATCH: metadata-only changes or bugfixes with no expected output impact
- status: active | deprecated | disabled
- deprecation:
  - planned_end_of_support_date (required if status=deprecated)
  - replacement_model_id/version (optional)

Serving + compatibility constraints
- runtime:
  - engine_min_version (e.g., runtime-1.18.0)
  - supported_backends (e.g., triton, vllm-like runtime path) (enumerated list)
  - kv_cache_compat: explicit flag if incompatible cache format changes
- tokenizer:
  - tokenizer_id or tokenizer_sha (required)
  - tokenizer_revision (optional)
- interfaces:
  - supported_tasks: chat | completion | embeddings | rerank
  - supports_streaming: true/false
  - supports_tool_calling: true/false
  - structured_output: none | json_schema | grammar

Variants / quantization profiles
- variants: list of served variants
  - variant_id (immutable)
  - precision: fp16 | bf16 | int8 | int4
  - quantization:
    - method (e.g., awq, gptq, smoothquant)
    - constraints (notes on max seq len, performance caveats)
  - context_window_tokens
  - max_output_tokens (policy default / guardrail default)

Deployment availability + rollout eligibility
- availability:
  - hosted: available | limited | unavailable
  - dedicated: available | limited | unavailable
  - private: available | limited | unavailable
- rollout_policy:
  - eligible_for_autopromote: true/false
  - requires_manual_approval: true/false (esp. Private)
  - fallback_targets: ordered list of compatible model_id/version ranges

Quality/safety notes (public + internal separation)
- public_release_notes: short customer-facing bullets (subject to redaction rules)
- safety_notes_public: allowed, generic (e.g., “updated refusal behavior for self-harm content”)
- internal_notes: internal-only, must never publish to docs/Console non-admin
- evals:
  - eval_run_ids (internal)
  - quality_summary_public (optional, must follow style guide and significance requirements)

Validation tooling deliverables
- JSON Schema (authoritative) committed in registry repo
- Fixture payloads:
  - at least 3 model families + at least 2 quantization variants
  - one deprecated example with required deprecation fields present
  - one “Private unavailable” example
- CLI or script used by CI to validate:
  - schema conformance
  - semantic version format
  - invariants:
    - if status=deprecated => planned_end_of_support_date present
    - if availability.private=available => runtime.engine_min_version present (Private bundles require pinned runtime)
    - no public_release_notes contain restricted markers (see ENG-9825)

Acceptance criteria
- Schema v1 is merged and referenced by ADR-0142 publishing workflow.
- CI fails on invalid metadata with actionable error output (field path + reason).
- Fixtures added and used in tests.
- Documentation in-repo:
  - “Required fields for launch” section
  - “Public vs internal fields” section (links to ENG-9825)
  - “How to add a new model/variant” quick checklist

Implementation plan
1) Draft schema v1 in model registry repo (Quentin)
2) Add validator script + unit tests (Sahana)
3) Add CI job + required check (Sahana + Connor review for release gates)
4) Add fixtures and golden tests for backwards compatibility of schema changes

Risks / open questions
- How strict should semver enforcement be for early backfill? Proposal: strict for any *new* or *changed* records after cutover; grandfather legacy via migration path in ENG-9822.
- Compat constraint language: keep minimal for v1 (exact version pins + simple ranges), defer richer expressions until rollout policy engine needs it.
- Public quality summaries: must not claim improvements without statistical backing (coordinate with Jonas/Sana; downstream gating in ENG-9827).
